art.subject: Godlewski's Bunting (Emberiza godlewskii), adult male, a vagrant on a rocky hillside in Korea in early spring: head, throat and breast pale blue-grey; a chestnut stripe along each side of the crown and a chestnut stripe behind the eye; a short blackish line on the lores in front of the eye; a dark moustachial stripe, blackish from the base of the bill, outlining the grey ear coverts; mantle rufous-brown with bold blackish streaks; rump unstreaked chestnut; wings with black-centred, rufous-fringed coverts and tertials; belly and flanks warm cinnamon-rufous; tail dark with white outer feathers. Bill grey and conical; eye dark; legs pinkish.
art.pose: hopping on a rock among dry grass, side view
art.scene: dry rocky hillside with sparse grass and bare shrubs in Korea in early spring (March), clear light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A medium-sized, long-tailed bunting, a little larger than a sparrow, slim with a rounded head; no crest, the crown feathers lie flat. Hops on rocks and bare ground. Bill small, conical, grey, shorter than the head. Legs pinkish, medium length. The long, notched tail extends well beyond the wingtips and has white outer feathers.
avoid: Do not paint black crown stripes or a black eye-stripe — that is Rock Bunting (Emberiza cia); Godlewski's crown and eye-stripes are chestnut, only the lores and the front of the moustache are blackish.
Do not paint a white face and white throat with dark stripes — that is Meadow Bunting, common in Korea; Godlewski's face and throat are grey.
Do not paint a streaked rump; it is plain chestnut.
